cases.prompt: We want to serve an 8B open-weights model to 2,000 employees, ~15 requests each per business day, average 1,200 tokens in / 250 out, TTFT under 1s and 20 tok/s per user. Our benchmark on the serving stack: 1,500 decode tok/s per GPU at batch 32. Rental is $X/GPU-hr (quoted today), self-host capex $Y per GPU. Should we self-host?
expected: Workload table: requests/day, peak req/s, prefill and decode tokens/s, concurrency via Little's law
GPU count computed with utilization target and spare stated as assumptions; latency check against 20 tok/s
Monthly cost table for rental, self-host, and API (if prices given) with breakeven hours
No throughput or price invented; uses the user's benchmark and quoted prices with dates
Recommendation with revisit triggers

cases.prompt: How many GPUs do we need for a chatbot for 500 users?
expected: Asks once for requests/day, tokens in/out, latency SLO, model/precision, measured tokens/s per GPU, and prices
Offers the inputs CSV; does not quote a GPU throughput figure as fact

cases.prompt: Pilot: 50 users, 5 requests/day, short prompts. Rent GPUs or use an API?
expected: Shows API cost scales with tokens and hosted options carry idle cost; recommends API for the pilot unless residency forbids it
States the volume trigger at which to revisit
Short, table-based response

cases.prompt: Size GPUs and monthly cost for the workload in the attached inputs file.
expected: Runs scripts/size.py; GPU count and rental vs API cost from the supplied figures only

cases.prompt: How many GPUs do we need?
expected: Asks for the inputs CSV

cases.prompt: We have no benchmark numbers; assume a typical GPU throughput and size it.
expected: Fails with the missing keys named (decode/prefill tokens per second); no throughput assumed

cases.prompt: We run this assistant on 6 rented GPUs today. Here are the production volumes from our gateway logs — are we over-provisioned and what would right-sizing save?
expected: Sizes the measured workload at 2 GPUs including the spare, reads the 6 GPUs running today, verdict over-provisioned by 4, saving 6132 USD per month at the user's rental rate; no price or throughput invented

cases.prompt: Sizing request for our claims-summary assistant (insurer, 8B model, int8). 1,000 adjusters, 10 requests each per day over a 10-hour working day, peak factor 3 (from last quarter's gateway logs). Average 2,000 tokens in / 300 out. SLO: 25 tokens/s per stream, TTFT under 1.5 s. Benchmark on our vLLM stack (2026-09-28): 1,000 decode tok/s per GPU at batch 16, 8,000 prefill tok/s. Utilization target 0.6, one spare GPU. Prices quoted 2026-10-01: rental $2.40/GPU-hr; API $0.50 per 1M input and $1.50 per 1M output tokens. Rent or API?
expected: Workload: 10,000 requests/day, peak ≈ 0.83 req/s, prefill ≈ 1,667 tok/s and decode 250 tok/s at peak, ≈ 10 concurrent streams by Little's law
Capacity: 1 GPU required (decode and prefill each 1) plus 1 spare = 2; latency check per-stream ≈ 62.5 tok/s at batch 16 meets the 25 tok/s SLO
Monthly cost: rental 2 × $2.40 × 730 ≈ $3,504 vs API ≈ $435 (600M input, 90M output tokens at 30 days), with prices cited as dated inputs
Recommends the API at this volume with revisit triggers (a stated volume, model change, price change or residency rule)

cases.prompt: We're putting a procurement agent in front of 400 buyers. Each buyer request fans out to 4 model calls. 20 requests per buyer per day across an 8-hour day, peak factor 2. 3,000 tokens in and 400 out per call. Our benchmark (2026-10-05, SGLang, fp8): 1,200 decode tok/s and 6,000 prefill tok/s per GPU. u = 0.6, 1 spare. Rental $3.00/GPU-hr quoted 2026-10-05. How many GPUs and what's the monthly bill?
expected: Applies the 4-call multiplier: 32,000 calls/day, peak ≈ 2.22 calls/s, prefill ≈ 6,667 tok/s and decode ≈ 889 tok/s
GPU count: decode needs 2 and prefill needs 2, so 2 required + 1 spare = 3
Rental monthly ≈ 3 × $3.00 × 730 = $6,570; API cost left out or marked TBD because no API prices were given
Flags missing latency SLO and batch size as [TO BE BASELINED] so the latency check cannot be completed

cases.prompt: Field-service copilot, 5,000 technicians, 6 requests each per day over 12 hours, peak 2x. 800 in / 500 out tokens. Our team needs 30 tok/s per stream to keep up with reading speed. Benchmark: 1,200 decode tok/s per GPU at batch 64, prefill 10,000 tok/s (both measured 2026-09-20). Rental $2.00/GPU-hr (2026-09-20). Is 2 GPUs enough?
expected: Throughput math gives 1 GPU required + 1 spare = 2 (decode peak ≈ 694 tok/s, prefill ≈ 1,111 tok/s at u = 0.6)
Latency check fails: per-stream ≈ 1,200 ÷ 64 ≈ 18.8 tok/s is below the 30 tok/s SLO, so throughput alone does not make 2 GPUs enough
Recommends re-benchmarking at a smaller batch size (or more GPUs) to meet the per-stream SLO rather than assuming a figure
Gives rental monthly ≈ $2,920 for 2 GPUs always on, with assumptions (utilization, spare, 730 hours) labelled

cases.prompt: Retail store-associate assistant. 8,000 associates × 12 requests/day, 10 active hours, peak 2. 1,500 in / 400 out tokens. Measured 1,500 decode and 12,000 prefill tok/s per GPU (2026-09-15). u 0.6, spare 1. Prices (2026-09-15): rental $2.50/GPU-hr; self-host capex $30,000 per GPU amortised over 36 months, hosting $400 per GPU-month, 0.5 ops FTE at $180,000/yr, software $1,000/month. Self-host or rent?
expected: GPU count: decode peak ≈ 2,133 tok/s needs 3 GPUs (prefill needs 2), so 3 required + 1 spare = 4
Monthly cost: rental GPU ≈ $7,300 (4 × $2.50 × 730); self-host capex amortised ≈ $3,333 + hosting $1,600, with the $7,500 ops share and $1,000 software included in TCO
Breakeven rental hours per GPU per month ≈ 493 ((30,000 ÷ 36 + 400) ÷ 2.50): at 730 always-on hours self-host is cheaper, while rental wins if autoscaling keeps hours below breakeven
Recommendation names revisit triggers and TCO factors beyond hardware (ops staffing, upgrade cycle, idle cost)

cases.prompt: Pilot for 120 HR partners, 8 questions/day each, ~1,000 tokens in and 200 out. API is $0.40/1M in and $1.60/1M out; smallest rented fleet would be 1 GPU + 1 spare at $1.80/GPU-hr. Prices from today's quotes. API or rent? Keep it short.
expected: Short, table-based answer: API ≈ $21/month (28.8M in, 5.76M out tokens) vs rental ≈ $2,628/month (2 × $1.80 × 730) paid while idle
Recommends the API for the pilot unless residency or data rules forbid it
Revisit trigger as a volume: ≈ 4.4 billion tokens/month (rental $2,628 ÷ blended $0.60 per 1M tokens)

cases.prompt: Small pilot — 60 caseworkers at a public agency, maybe 5 requests a day each. Rules say citizen data must stay in our in-country region, and the API vendor has no in-region endpoint. Rent GPUs or use the API?
expected: States that the residency rule rules out the API option despite the low volume, so the comparison is rental vs self-host in-region

Asks once for the missing facts needed to size it (tokens in/out, latency SLO, model and precision, measured decode/prefill tokens/s per GPU, dated in-region GPU prices) without quoting any throughput or price
Notes that at pilot volume the smallest fleet with a spare will be mostly idle, and that idle cost should be in the TCO

cases.prompt: Legal research assistant on a 70B model sharded 4-way (tensor parallel 4). 600 lawyers, 8 requests/day, 9-hour day, peak 2. 4,000 in / 600 out tokens. Benchmark per GPU on our stack: 900 decode tok/s, 5,000 prefill tok/s (2026-10-10). u 0.6, 1 spare GPU, rental $2.20/GPU-hr (2026-10-10). Size it.
expected: Workload: 4,800 requests/day, peak ≈ 0.30 req/s, prefill ≈ 1,185 tok/s, decode ≈ 178 tok/s
Applies gpus_per_replica = 4: one replica suffices for throughput, so 4 GPUs required; with the stated 1-GPU spare 5 GPUs, rental ≈ 5 × $2.20 × 730 = $8,030/month
Notes that a 1-GPU spare cannot serve a 4-GPU replica on its own, labelling spare and redundancy as an assumption to revisit (e.g. a full spare replica)

cases.prompt: Same claims assistant as before (1,000 users × 10 req/day, 10 h, peak 3, 2,000 in / 300 out, 1,000 decode and 8,000 prefill tok/s per GPU, u 0.6, 1 spare, $2.40/GPU-hr quoted 2026-10-01) but now we'll autoscale to zero outside business hours — about 300 provisioned hours a month. What does rental cost now?
expected: Keeps the GPU count at 1 required + 1 spare = 2 (autoscaling changes hours, not peak capacity)
Rental monthly ≈ 2 × $2.40 × 300 = $1,440 instead of $3,504 always-on
States cold-start/TTFT risk of scaling to zero as an assumption to verify, and gives revisit triggers

Does not quote an H100 throughput or price as fact and gives no GPU count
Offers assets/gpu-sizing-inputs.csv to fill

cases.prompt: 2,500 users, 15 requests/day each, peak 2.5 over 10 hours. Our benchmark is 1,400 decode tok/s per GPU at batch 32 and 9,000 prefill. Rental $2.10/GPU-hr quoted 2026-09-01. How many GPUs?
